Off. Android doesn’t let an app move a call to the speaker directly, so the app presses the call screen’s Speaker button for you. For that, turn on “Alo Answer: speaker” in Accessibility.
On: after answering, the app presses the Speaker button on the call screen.

This phone doesn’t allow changing the phone app.

Make Alo Answer your phone app, and it handles calls itself: the most reliable voice answer, and the speaker turns on directly (no accessibility tricks). It replaces the phone app’s call screens and dial pad; you can switch back any time in Settings → Apps → Default apps.
On. Alo Answer shows the call screen itself: say “allo” and it answers and turns on the speaker directly. Auto speaker and “Display over other apps” aren’t needed.
On: when the phone rings, say “alo” to answer
Preparing the speech model (first start takes a few seconds)…
No events yet. They appear here when a call rings.
These steps are for Xiaomi, Redmi and POCO phones. This phone reports itself as %1$s.
Alo Answer needs these to pick up calls when you say “alo”. Each one is used only for what is written under it.
In the list that opens, find Alo Answer and turn the switch on, then come back.
Lets the app pick up the ringing call after you say “alo”.
Listens for “alo” only while the phone is ringing (at most 30 seconds) or during a test. Speech is recognized offline on the phone itself; the app has no internet access and does not save the audio.
Android shows a notification whenever the microphone is open. The app also uses notifications to tell you when voice answering could not start, and why.

Android lets an app use the microphone in the background only if listening was started while the app was on screen. So when the phone rings, the app shows an invisible screen for under a second to start listening. Opening that screen needs this permission.
Lets the app notice when the phone starts ringing, gets answered or hangs up. The caller\'s number is never read.
You chose “Don\'t allow” earlier, so Android won\'t ask again. Open Settings → Permissions and allow it there.
Higher: catches “alo” more easily but answers by mistake more often. Lower: fewer mistakes, but you may need to repeat yourself. Applies from the next call or test.
The app pressed the Speaker button on the call screen, and Android confirms the call audio is on the loudspeaker.
As the default phone app, Alo Answer switched the call to the loudspeaker itself.
The call was answered but stayed on the earpiece as far as Android reports. Turn on “Auto speaker” below, so the app presses the call screen’s Speaker button for you.

A Bluetooth device or headset was connected, so the call stayed on it, as on any phone. The loudspeaker is turned on only when nothing is connected. You can switch on the call screen with the audio button.
After the app answers a call, the result of the speaker attempt shows here.
This only means Android accepted the request. An app that is not your phone app cannot reliably control the call\'s audio, so check by ear whether the last call really came out of the loudspeaker.
Android says the speaker was selected
Settings → Apps → Manage apps → Alo Answer → Autostart
Without Autostart, HyperOS usually doesn\'t wake the app up for system events such as an incoming call.
Settings → Apps → Manage apps → Alo Answer → Battery saver → No restrictions
Stops HyperOS from freezing the app while it waits for calls.
Open the app, open Recents, long-press the Alo Answer card and tap the lock icon
Optional: lock the app in Recents
Makes HyperOS less likely to clear the app from memory.
Settings → Apps → Manage apps → Alo Answer → Other permissions
Other permissions: pop-up windows + lock screen
Xiaomi adds its own switches that block the invisible listening screen. Turn on “Display pop-up windows while running in the background” and “Show on Lock screen”.
Settings → Apps → Manage apps → Alo Answer → Display over other apps
The Android permission that lets the app open its listening screen while the phone rings.
A call is ringing right now. Try the test after it ends.

Listens for up to 60 seconds and never answers anything. During a real call the ringtone plays next to the microphone, which can make “alo” harder to catch than it is here. Also try it from a meter or two away.
Couldn\'t open settings. Use the path shown.
The Xiaomi screen wasn\'t found on this version, so a general Android settings screen opened instead. Use the path shown.
Menu names differ between MIUI and HyperOS versions. If a button lands on the wrong screen, follow the path instead. Then test with a real call from another phone and check the Event log.
HyperOS stops background apps much more aggressively than plain Android. Without these settings the phone may ring and nothing happens.
